reason: The passage exemplifies the stated leadership model through God's actions: (1) responsibility for welfare—God provides manna (bread from heaven) and establishes the Sabbath to ensure the people's sustenance and rest; (2) accountability for actions—God explicitly tests the people's obedience ('לְמַעַן אֲנַסֶּנּוּ—'to test you'), rebukes them for not keeping commandments ('עַד־ אָנָה מֵֽאַנְתֶּם לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתַי—'How long will you refuse to keep my commandments'), and holds them accountable by withholding manna on the seventh day when they disregard the Sabbath. In biblical context, God is presented as the model for authority, making this passage a demonstration of the leadership principle stated.
